therefore $\angle 1=\angle 2=45^\circ$,\\
since $MN \perp BC$,\\
therefore $\angle ENC=\angle ENB=90^\circ$,\\
therefore quadrilateral MNCD is a rectangle,\\
therefore $MN=CD=6$, $DM=CN$, $\angle DME=90^\circ$,\\
in $\triangle CDE$ and $\triangle CBE$,\\

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the diagram, in square $ABCD$, $AB=6$, $E$ is a point on the diagonal $AC$, and line $BE$ is drawn. Through point $E$, line $EF\perp BE$ intersects $AD$ at point $F$. The areas of $\triangle BCE$ and $\triangle AEF$ are $S_1$ and $S_2$, respectively. If $2S_1=3S_2$, then what is the length of $CE$?
raw_record.answer: Solution: Connect $ED$, and through $E$ draw $MN \perp BC$ at $N$, intersecting $AD$ at $M$. Since quadrilateral $ABCD$ is a square, therefore $AB=BC=CD=AD=6$, $\angle ABC=\angle BCD=\angle ADC=\angle DAB=90^\circ$. Therefore $\angle 1=\angle 2=45^\circ$. Since $MN \perp BC$, therefore $\angle ENC=\angle ENB=90^\circ$. Therefore quadrilateral $MNCD$ is a rectangle, so $MN=CD=6$, $DM=CN$, and $\angle DME=90^\circ$. In $\triangle CDE$ and $\triangle CBE$, $CD=CB$, $\angle 2=\angle 1$, and $CE=CE$, therefore $\triangle CDE \cong \triangle CBE$ (SAS). Therefore $ED=EB$ and $\angle EDC=\angle EBC$. Since $\angle CDA=\angle CBA=90^\circ$, therefore $\angle CDA-\angle EDC=\angle CBA-\angle EBC$, that is $\angle ADE=\angle ABE$. Since $EF \perp BE$, therefore $\angle FEB=90^\circ$. Since $\angle FEB+\angle DAB+\angle AFE+\angle ABE=360^\circ$, therefore $\angle AFE+\angle ABE=360^\circ-\angle FEB-\angle DAB=180^\circ$. Since $\angle AFE+\angle EFD=180^\circ$, therefore $\angle ABE=\angle EFD$. Therefore $\angle ADE=\angle EFD$, so $ED=EF$. Since $\angle DME=90^\circ$, therefore $EM \perp DF$, so $DM=MF$. In $\triangle NEC$, $\angle 1=45^\circ$, therefore $\triangle NEC$ is an isosceles right triangle. Let $NE=NC=x$. Then $CE=\sqrt{2}x$, $DM=MF=CN=x$, therefore $AF=AD-DM-MF=6-2x$, and $ME=MN-EN=6-x$. Therefore $S_1=\frac{1}{2}BC\cdot EN=\frac{1}{2}\times 6\times x=3x$, and $S_2=\frac{1}{2}(6-2x)(6-x)=x^2-9x+18$. Since $2S_1=3S_2$, therefore $2\cdot 3x=3(x^2-9x+18)$. Solving, we find $x_1=2$, $x_2=9$ (discard). Therefore $CE=\sqrt{2}x=2\sqrt{2}$. Hence, $CE=\boxed{2\sqrt{2}}$.
